entry.title: Voyager 1 Light-Day Mission Update and Conversation

media:group.media:title: Voyager 1 Light-Day Mission Update and Conversation
media:group.media:description:
We're making history with our Voyager spacecraft. Join us for the latest updates.
In this discussion, NASA leadership and mission members will discuss the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes are gathering in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping them operating for so long over such vast distances.
Stick around for a Q&A with media and other audience members, as well as a preview of the upcoming NASA+ Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027 for the mission's 50th anniversary.
Participants include: - Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters - Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA JPL, and professor of planetary science, Caltech - Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL - Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist, NASA JPL - Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL - Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University
Voyager 1, the most distant human-made object from Earth, will have traveled one light-day (more than 16 billion light-years) as of Wednesday, Nov. 18. Learn more about the milestone: https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-invites-media-public-to-join-voyager-1-one-light-day-activities/
Learn more about NASA's Voyager mission: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Undocking

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Undocking
media:group.media:description:
Watch as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft undocks from the International Space Station and begins its journey back to Earth. The uncrewed Dragon is carrying scientific research samples and hardware including a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct and frozen microbial samples.
The spacecraft will reenter Earth's atmosphere Nov. 21 and will splash down off the Californian coast at approximately 5:04 p.m. EST (2:04 p.m. PST, 2204 UTC).
Learn more about NASA's SpaceX CRS-35 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crs-35/ Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

entry.title: MAX POWER: Highlights from NASA’s First-Ever Tech Expo and Air Show

media:group.media:title: MAX POWER: Highlights from NASA’s First-Ever Tech Expo and Air Show
media:group.media:description:
Relive the best moments from MAX POWER, NASA's first-ever tech expo and air show at and around Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Thousands gathered over several days in early November for NASA's first exhibition of America's superiority in space, aeronautics, and technology. The family-friendly event honored the nation's 250th anniversary and capped off the agency's Inspiration Tour.
Highlights from the first-ever MAX POWER included flyovers, a skydive by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, and a visit from President Donald J. Trump. NASA also unveiled a new X-plane, opened recruitment for astronaut candidates, and launched a student Moon Base challenge, while sharing the agency’s latest lunar exploration plans.
Learn more: https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower/ https://www.nasa.gov/general/max-power-nasas-inaugural-aerospace-expo-ignites-americas-future/
Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/MAX%20POWER%20Highlights%20from%20NASA's%20First-Ever%20Tech%20Expo%20and%20Air%20Show

entry.title: NASA Expands Lunar Delivery Network to Support Moon Base Development

media:group.media:title: NASA Expands Lunar Delivery Network to Support Moon Base Development
media:group.media:description:
Establishing a sustained human presence on the Moon will require a steady flow of scientific instruments, new technologies, equipment, and infrastructure to the lunar surface.
NASA has selected eight American companies for the next phase of its CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative, expanding the network of commercial providers eligible for future lunar delivery missions.
Building on NASA's existing lunar delivery capabilities, this expansion will help increase the frequency of deliveries to the lunar surface and support the growing demands of Moon Base development.
With each lunar delivery, NASA is building toward a future of sustained human exploration and scientific discovery on the Moon.
Learn more about Moon Base: https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/

media:group.media:title: U.S. Spacewalk 101
media:group.media:description:
On Thursday, Nov. 5, NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will install and deploy the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA), completing the space station's power system augmentation. Together, the eight roll-out arrays will increase the station's available power by up to 30%.
The spacewalk is scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 UTC) and will last around six and a half hours.
Learn more about this spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97 Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

entry.title: Astronaut Anil Menon Speaks With Mark Rober From the International Space Station

media:group.media:title: Astronaut Anil Menon Speaks With Mark Rober From the International Space Station
media:group.media:description:
Join us as NASA astronaut Anil Menon, currently aboard the International Space Station, speaks with Mark Rober of the ClassCrunchLabs Foundation in advance of National STEM Day.
During this live event, Rober and Menon will discuss questions submitted by students about the station and life in space. Menon will also demonstrate how everyday activities, from eating to experimenting, change in microgravity.
Learn more about how your school or community could speak with astronauts aboard the station: https://www.nasa.gov/stemonstation

media:group.media:title: U.S. Spacewalk 100
media:group.media:description:
Join us for a spacewalk milestone!
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk are participating in the 100th spacewalk conducted from the International Space Station's Quest airlock without the space shuttle present. This will be the 285th spacewalk conducted to build, maintain, and upgrade the orbiting laboratory.
Menon and Kutryk are expected to begin their spacewalk at about 8:00 a.m. EDT (1200 UTC); they'll be installing a new International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (IROSA), which will boost the station's power.
Learn more about today's spacewalk: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97 Get daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

media:group.media:title: Artemis Acceleration (Oct. 23, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Tune in as agency leaders provide an update on NASA's plans to return American astronauts to the surface of the Moon by 2028.
Participants include: - NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman - NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya - Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager
As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Moon missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.
More about the Artemis program: https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/

entry.title: Live High-Definition Views from the International Space Station (Official NASA Stream)

media:group.media:title: Live High-Definition Views from the International Space Station (Official NASA Stream)
media:group.media:description:
Live views from the International Space Station are streaming from an external camera mounted on the station's Harmony module.
The camera is looking forward at an angle so that International Docking Adapter 2 is visible. If the Harmony module camera is not available due to operational considerations for a longer period of time, a continuous loop of recorded Earth views will be displayed with the caption “Previously Recorded.”
The space station orbits Earth about 250 miles (425 kilometers) above the surface. An international partnership of five space agencies from 15 countries operates the station, and it has been continuously occupied since November 2000. It's a microgravity laboratory where science, research, and human innovation make way for new technologies and research breakthroughs not possible on Earth. More: https://go.nasa.gov/3CkVtC8
Did you know you can spot the station without a telescope? It looks like a fast-moving star, but you have to know when to look up. Download our mobile app for alerts to let you know when (and where) to spot the station and wave to the crew: https://www.nasa.gov/spot-the-station/
https://nasa.gov/iss
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:description:

NASA participants in the news conference include: - Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, Low Earth Orbit Program - Garrett Hehn, spacewalk flight director, Flight Operations Directorate
Learn more about the spacewalks: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97 Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station

entry.title: NASA Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles (October 2026 Update)

media:group.media:title: NASA Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles (October 2026 Update)
media:group.media:description:
There's a lot of ground to cover when you're building a Moon Base.
From robotic rovers exploring the rugged lunar landscape to lunar terrain vehicles carrying Artemis astronauts across the surface, mobility will play a crucial role in establishing an enduring human presence on the Moon.
During the early phases of Moon Base development, these vehicles will help NASA investigate the lunar South Pole region, conduct scientific research, test new technologies, and gather the information that will inform future missions.
In this Moon Base update, get a closer look at some of the lunar terrain vehicles and robotic rovers helping pave the way for humanity's first lunar outpost.
Learn more about these vehicles: https://www.nasa.gov/missions/moon-base/nasa-provides-progress-update-on-moon-base-rovers/ Learn more about Moon Base: https://www.nasa.gov/moonbase/ Download this video: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Moon_Base_Update-Oct-Lunar_Rovers
